newsitem.title: RWANDA: U.N. envoy Chretien in Rwanda for Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy Chretien in Rwanda for Zaire talks.

text.p: U.N. special envoy Raymond Chretien arrived in the Rwandan capital Kigali on Friday for talks with the country's two most powerful men, whose cooperation is vital for any outside mission to aid refugees in Zaire.

"I am here to discuss the situation in eastern Zaire with the president and the defence minister," the Canadian diplomat told a news conference shortly after his Canadian air force jet touched down from Nairobi in Kenya where he spent the night.

He said his talks with President Pasteur Bizimungu, a Hutu in the Tutsi-led government, and with key Tutsi Defence Minister Paul Kagame would deal with deployment of a U.N.-sanctioned force in Zaire and the continued fighting there.
"I will be listening to their Rwandan viewpoints. I will look at their perception of the conflict," Chretien said.
U.N. officials said Chretien changed his original plans to go first to the Zairean capital Kinshasa after a meeting in France with ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko.

Mobutu gave Chretien his blessing for plans for foreign intervention to help 1.2 million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees in his country and told the envoy a visit to Rwanda would therefore be more fruitful, they said.
Rwandan support for a protection force is vital as the easiest supply routes pass through its territory and the rebels who have seized a chunk of eastern Zaire are allies of Rwanda.
